insights.insight: The network has verified 17,193 actual transactions totaling $1.07M in GMV — not modeled audiences, not intent signals, but cryptographically confirmed purchases spanning physical retail, dining, fuel, warehouse, and digital SaaS. For brands paying $5+ CPM for probabilistic targeting, this is the structural alternative: a receipt is a closed loop, not an inference.

insights.topic: Category breadth now includes digital commerce
insights.insight: Google entered the top-brand list on April 28, marking the first time a digital commerce provider appeared in the 14-day brand rankings — a category that was entirely absent before April 9. The network now spans physical-to-digital purchase verification, which expands its utility beyond CPG and retail into subscription and SaaS audience targeting.

insights.topic: Throughput compression is real but appears to be flooring
insights.insight: Weekly GMV has dropped 64% from its $210K peak on April 13 to a current $76.5K band, and velocity hit an all-time low of 0.61x on April 30 — but the series has shown intraday stabilization in a $66K–$81K range over the past five days with no zero-inflow heartbeats. Brands evaluating data volume commitments should treat current throughput as the working baseline, not the peak.

The network hit 29 active metros on April 19 and recorded a 17-CBSA single-heartbeat expansion — the highest geographic diffusion rate in its history at 81%. For marketers requiring regional or local purchase verification, the addressable footprint has grown materially and quickly, though it has since settled back to 18 active metros in the current reading.

insights.topic: Intraday receipt flow follows a predictable cycle
insights.insight: Across multiple consecutive days, the 16:15–20:15 UTC window consistently produces the highest receipt volumes, with 00:15 cycles as structural troughs. This pattern is stable enough to inform how brands should time data pulls or audience refreshes if integrating this signal into campaign activation workflows.

insights.topic: Lightning micropayment layer is live but nascent
insights.insight: 253 Lightning payouts have been made against 17,193 receipts — a 1.5% claim rate — with 6.7M sats distributed at 129 sats per receipt at current BTC pricing. The incentive layer is functional but underutilized, which means the existing verified GMV was generated largely without financial inducement, reducing the selection-bias concern that often undermines incentivized receipt programs.
